data.body:
IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 1234 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1234). Three files:
the two NEW DC convergence suites plus a provenance-COMMENT-only change to
adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py. Cloud's two convergence files are BYTE-UNCHANGED
(`git diff origin/main -- <both>` is empty). Module sizes: backend.py 350 -> 371 (cap 800);
new suites 234 and 241 LOC.

THE PLAN'S SPECIFICS ALL HELD — every one of the five rounds' findings was load-bearing in
practice, not just in principle. Recording the proofs.

DESCRIPTION SUITE — value discriminator, as the plan specified. All THREE of outbound_mapper=,
inbound_mapper= and links= bound to a real JiraDataCenterBackend over FakeTransport, via one
`_compute` helper so no call site can forget one. Landed description is exactly 32767 plain chars
and ends with " … [truncated by reconciler]"; pass 2 over that body plans zero description
updates; the local ticket keeps its full 40000 chars.

COMMENT SUITE — identity + recording, NOT value, exactly as round 4(b) required. `_diff_comments`
called DIRECTLY with `sanitizer=` and `inbound_mapper=` (both have their own config fallback).
The injected DC sanitizer is wrapped in a `RecordingSanitizer` that delegates every member
untouched (`__getattr__`) and records `fit_comment` calls. Two assertions carry the proof:
`recorder.wrapped is dc_backend.sanitizer` (identity) and `recorder.fit_comment_calls` non-empty
in BOTH passes (recording) — pass 2's zero-mutation result is only accepted if the injected
sanitizer actually ran, so it cannot be a zero produced by a bypass.

ONE ADDITION BEYOND THE PLAN, because the first draft had a hole the plan did not name. Both
suites originally asserted the landed length against WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT — the very constant
under test. That made them SELF-CONSISTENT under a raised limit: mutating 32767 -> 400000 left the
convergence assertion green, because the fixture "Jira" stored whatever rebar sent. So each suite
now spells Jira's real ceiling as a LITERAL `_JIRA_TEXT_FIELD_CHARACTER_LIMIT = 32767` (a fact
about the instance, which does not move when rebar's constant does) and routes pass 1's output
through `_as_jira_would_store()` before pass 2. With that, a loosened limit makes CONVERGENCE
ITSELF fail, not merely a length assertion. Verified below (MUT B2b / B-neutralized).

MUTATION LEDGER — every verdict an AssertionError, never an AttributeError/ImportError:

MUTATED: dropped outbound_mapper=/inbound_mapper=/links= from the description suite's `_compute`
  (i.e. let the OR-guarded config fallback resolve the backend);
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_description_converges_over_two_passes —
  "AssertionError: DC must fit the description to Jira's plain-character ceiling … assert 31887 ==
  32767". 31887 is Cloud's ADF fit. This is the round-3/round-4(a) finding reproduced exactly: the
  fallback resolves CLOUD and the cell would otherwise have been green while testing the wrong
  deployment.

MUTATED: dropped BOTH sanitizer= and inbound_mapper= from the comment suite's `_diff`;
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_comment_converges_over_two_passes —
  "AssertionError: The injected DC sanitizer was never consulted: _diff_comments fell back to
  select_backend(load_config()).sanitizer, so this pass compared bodies with CLOUD's fit while
  claiming to test DC." Note what did NOT happen: no exception, and the convergence assertion
  itself still passed — byte-identical output under both sanitizers, precisely as round 4(b)
  predicted. Only the recording check caught it.

MUTATED: dropped ONLY sanitizer= from the comment suite's `_diff`, keeping inbound_mapper=;
  FAILED: same test, same recording AssertionError. Confirms `_resolve_sanitizer` is an
  independent fallback and injecting the mapper does not cover it.

MUTATED: WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT 32767 -> 400000 (limit raised above the real ceiling);
  FAILED: test_dc_description_fit_is_a_plain_character_truncation — "assert 400000 == 32767";
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_description_converges_over_two_passes — ceiling AssertionError;
  FAILED: test_dc_comment_fit_targets_the_documented_instance_ceiling — "assert 400000 == 32767";
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_comment_converges_over_two_passes — "The landed comment must carry the
  visible truncation marker …".

MUTATED: WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT -> 400000 with the earlier length/marker assertions neutralized,
  to prove the CONVERGENCE assertion is itself sensitive rather than shadowed;
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_description_converges_over_two_passes — "Pass 2 must emit ZERO
  description updates (convergence)…";
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_comment_converges_over_two_passes — "Pass 2 must emit ZERO comment
  mutations (convergence)…". This is the check the `_as_jira_would_store` addition bought.

MUTATED: WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound reduced to `return text` (fit removed);
  FAILED: test_dc_description_fit_is_a_plain_character_truncation — "assert 40000 == 32767";
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_description_converges_over_two_passes — ceiling AssertionError;
  FAILED: test_dc_comment_fit_targets_the_documented_instance_ceiling — "assert 38015 == 32767";
  FAILED: test_oversize_dc_comment_converges_over_two_passes — marker AssertionError.

NO PRODUCTION BEHAVIOUR CHANGED. The sanitizer= seam (ticket 21ca) was sufficient, as the plan
said it would be; threading sanitizer through compute_outbound_mutations was NOT attempted and
remains a separate question. The limit was neither changed nor made configurable
(049e-9fac-a821-4ea2). The provenance comment cites jira.text.field.character.limit + jpm.xml's
default-value 32767 + JRASERVER-28519, plus the two known limits of the binding (admin-
configurability -> 049e-9fac; fit_outbound being the DESCRIPTION fitter) and a pointer to the new
comment suite.
